gaps.sentence: This guidebook is really ___ for travellers (USE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of: useful. 'Useless' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: There are many ___ (SIMILAR) between the two languages.
gaps.explanation: 'Many' needs a plural countable noun: similarities (note the -ty to -ties spelling).

gaps.sentence: The festival celebrates ___ (CREATE) in every form.
gaps.explanation: 'Celebrates creativity' — the abstract quality noun follows the verb.

gaps.sentence: We must ___ our efforts to finish on time (STRONG).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: strengthen. A base verb follows 'must'.

gaps.sentence: Her answer was ___ , so we had to ask again (RELEVANT).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — it did not relate to the question
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'relevant' is 'irrelevant' (ir- before r). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.hint: person needed: someone who installs wiring
gaps.explanation: An electrician is the person who works with electricity; 'electric' and 'electrical' are adjectives.

gaps.sentence: The success of the launch rests on the ___ (RELY) of the supplier.
gaps.explanation: 'The reliability of the supplier' — the quality noun is needed after 'the'.
